title: Exploring the potential of LLM to enhance teaching plans through teaching simulation
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether large language models (LLMs) can support teachers—not students—by improving lesson planning before instruction takes place. The authors focus on a common challenge in teaching preparation: novice teachers often struggle to anticipate students’ misconceptions, learning difficulties, and the kinds of classroom interactions that reveal whether a lesson plan is effective. The study asks whether an LLM can improve teaching plans by simulating teacher–student interactions, generating teaching reflections, and then revising the original plan accordingly.

The intervention is a prompt-based workflow using GPT-4 (and, in one comparison condition, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) to enhance high school mathematics teaching plans. Starting from existing lesson plans, the model first simulates classroom dialogue involving students with varying ability levels and typical errors, then produces teaching reflections based on those simulated interactions, and finally refines the lesson plan using those reflections. The authors evaluate eight datasets of lesson plans, including LLM-generated plans, human expert-written plans, and plans written by pre-service teachers, with improvements produced through one or two rounds of LLM-based refinement. Human raters scored plans on a detailed framework covering problem chains, teaching activities, knowledge content, teaching methods, evaluation, interdisciplinarity, practical value, scope, and overall quality.

The context is high school mathematics in China. The evaluation corpus included 480 teaching plans drawn from 60 lessons across four knowledge modules: Algebra, Functions, Geometry, and Statistics. Human evaluation was carried out by mathematics teachers with teaching experience, and the paper compares baseline lesson plans against LLM-enhanced versions rather than measuring direct student learning outcomes. The workflow was implemented through web-based LLM interfaces rather than custom-coded systems, with the aim of keeping the approach accessible to ordinary teachers.

The main conclusion is that LLM-based simulation and reflection substantially improved the quality of teaching plans. In many dimensions, the refined plans matched or exceeded the quality of high-quality human-written plans, and plans originally written by pre-service teachers also improved notably after LLM enhancement. Performance varied by content area, with the strongest results in statistics and weaker performance in geometry, where visual reasoning is harder to support through text alone. Overall, the paper argues that LLMs can serve as useful pre-class rehearsal and lesson refinement tools for teachers, especially for instructional preparation, though further work is needed on challenging question design, disciplinary depth, and broader validation in authentic teaching settings.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-family large language model used for generating and revising text.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to generate high school mathematics teaching plans, simulate teacher-student classroom interactions, generate teaching reflections, and iteratively refine teaching plans (Datasets A, B, D, E, H).

findings.finding_summary: Human evaluation of N=480 teaching plans (240 before enhancement, 240 after enhancement) found that teaching plans enhanced with GPT-4 via simulation, reflection, and refinement scored higher across most evaluated dimensions than baseline plans. One-round GPT-4 enhanced plans (Dataset D) scored slightly higher than high-quality human-written plans (Dataset C), and two-round GPT-4 enhanced plans (Dataset E) surpassed high-quality human-written plans on most dimensions, with 12 dimensions achieving average scores above 6.8 on an 8-point Likert scale.
findings.measure: Manual teacher ratings on an 8-point Likert evaluation framework across 16 reported dimensions/19 indicators of teaching plan quality

findings.finding_summary: GPT-4 enhancement of pre-service teachers' plans (Dataset H) produced average scores across dimensions around 7 on an 8-point scale, exceeding high-quality teaching plans written by experienced human teachers and approaching the scores of plans improved through two rounds of GPT-4 enhancement. The paper reports especially high practical value for these enhanced real-world plans, with Dimension V1 (practical value) exceeding 7.
findings.measure: Manual teacher ratings of enhanced pre-service teacher teaching plans, including practical value dimension V1
findings.sample_size: N=60 teaching plans in Dataset H

findings.finding_summary: Within GPT-4 one-round enhanced plans (Dataset D), performance varied by knowledge module but improved across all four mathematics modules. In the Statistics module, 13 evaluation dimensions scored above 7 points, with several dimensions exceeding 7.3, while Algebra and Functions also outperformed human-written plans in 11 and 13 dimensions respectively; Geometry was comparatively lower, with most scores around 6.4.
findings.measure: Manual teacher ratings of mathematics teaching-plan quality by knowledge module (Algebra, Functions, Geometry, Statistics)

identified_tools.name: Claude
identified_tools.description: Anthropic Claude-family large language model used for generating and revising text.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as an alternative LLM to improve the GPT-generated teaching plans from Dataset A through one round of simulation/reflection-based refinement, producing Dataset F.

findings.finding_summary: Teaching plans improved by Claude in one round (Dataset F) achieved average scores around 6.5 on the 8-point evaluation scale, indicating improvement over baseline GPT-generated plans but slightly below high-quality human-written teaching plans (Dataset C). The paper also notes particularly strong Claude results on Dimension C3, introduction of disciplinary history and culture, where enhanced plans outperformed human teachers though average scores still remained below 5.
findings.measure: Manual teacher ratings on multidimensional teaching-plan quality framework
findings.sample_size: N=60 teaching plans in Dataset F

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical comparative study with structured human evaluation, but it is not a student-outcome RCT or QED. Outcomes are based on expert ratings of generated teaching plans rather than direct learning gains.
impact_tier_rationale: Results are consistently positive, but impact is based on rubric scores without reported effect sizes or direct student achievement outcomes. The magnitude appears meaningful yet remains unclear by the tier framework.
